rv.q: After all these years, Albin and Georges really are good together. The longtime couple at the center of the drag farce “ La Cage aux Folles ,” they haven’t always seemed that way.
For an evening at City Center, that proposition feels not merely persuasive but gloriously true.
It’s a reminder of how glorious La Cage aux Folles can be when everything clicks.
What makes this “Cage” worth seeing is Porter and Brady’s red-hot chemistry.
There are signs that O’Hara is indeed trying some new approaches, but the opening night performance offered more signs that the show, to put it charitably, hasn’t quite come together yet.
Indeed, the enterprise has to be declared entertaining, even if not thoroughly polished to a high gloss.
But Robert O’Hara’s production is rough, underdeveloped and fundamentally out of step with the show it is trying to reinvent.
But after its rousing opening number, O'Hara doesn't de-glam La Cage so much as completely flatline it.
It's a joy to hear Herman's bouncy score, performed with verve by a 30-piece orchestra under Joseph Joubert's baton.
Wayne Brady and Billy Porter give La Cage aux Folles everything they've got, but the production around them never decides what story it's telling.

cn.t: Porter and Brady's tender chemistry elevates this uneven Encores! revival, though O'Hara's all-Black reimagining struggles with rough execution and lacks urgency between Herman's still-joyous musical numbers.

vr.q: I highly recommend going to see La cage aux folles what a spectacular production.
The moment I will remember forever is Billy Porter singing I am what I am. Everyone was completely destroyed.
La Cage aux Folles at City Center is a must-see
an incredibly solid production LED by Billy Porter and Wayne Brady, and you have a show that feels like it is ready to go to Broadway tomorrow
